claim: For the deterministic predator–prey delay system (1) of Cui, Shao, Xue and Zhao with the Section 5 parameters \(f=1.5\), \(p=4\), \(a=4.8\), \(b=5\), \(c=2.1\), \(\mu=1.2\), \(d=0.1\), \(h=0.01\), \(k=0.9\), \(\alpha=0.6\), and with gestation delay \(\tau_2=0\), the positive equilibrium is \(E_*=(0.12190814516912455\ldots,0.57015890856106163\ldots)\). Its linearization reduces to \[\Delta(\lambda,\tau_1)=\lambda^2+P\lambda+Q+R e^{-\lambda\tau_1}=0,\] with \(P=0.08973289370238628\ldots\), \(Q=0.02066873788490888\ldots\), and \(R=0.02113947640068467\ldots\). Imaginary roots satisfy \(z^2+(P^2-2Q)z+(Q^2-R^2)=0\), with \(z=\omega^2\); this quadratic has exactly one positive root, giving \(\omega_*=0.18402882564735636\ldots\). The first phase-compatible crossing is \(\tau_{1,*}=4.87168883017987792\ldots\), and \(\operatorname{Re}(d\lambda/d\tau_1)=0.005780976092865250\ldots>0\) there. Because the zero-delay polynomial is Hurwitz and \(\Delta(0,\tau_1)=Q+R>0\) for every delay, the coexistence equilibrium is linearly asymptotically stable for \(0\le\tau_1<\tau_{1,*}\) and first loses linear stability at \(\tau_{1,*}\). Therefore the paper's reported Case II value \(\tau_1^*=4.5923\) is not a characteristic-root crossing of the printed model. Repeating the calculation with the paper's rounded equilibrium \((0.1219,0.5702)\) gives \(4.874589989058015\ldots\), so the discrepancy is not explained by equilibrium rounding. The paper's simulations at \(\tau_1=3.5\) and \(\tau_1=5\) remain qualitatively consistent with the corrected threshold. The claim is limited to the Case II linear threshold; it does not determine nonlinear Hopf criticality or the two-delay Case IV boundary.
integrity: The equilibrium and characteristic coefficients are reconstructed directly from the printed model. The unique positive imaginary frequency, phase-compatible first delay, zero-delay Hurwitz condition, absence of zero roots, positive crossing speed, and rounded-equilibrium robustness are independently replayed by the bundled numerical verifier.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns only local linear stability on the one-delay slice tau_2=0 at the source numerical parameter set.
It does not determine nonlinear Hopf criticality, global dynamics, or the two-delay stability boundary.
The literature comparison cannot exclude unindexed equivalent corrections.
title: Corrected first fear-delay Hopf threshold in a double-delay Beddington–DeAngelis model
